about: Repo notes: what the repository says exists, checked 2026-10-27; R14's den_lighting behaviour re-read from its working-checkout source on 2026-10-28 and 2026-10-29. Each note is source and dated receipts, not freshly queried live state. Paths are relative to C:\claude\home; 'origin/main:' means the committed main branch, which is newer than the shared checkout for these services.

notes.text: The occupancy gate is Frigate 0.18 on a Raspberry Pi 5 with a Hailo accelerator (hailo8l backend): whole-room person detection on the den camera at 1280×720, 10 fps, about 10–12 ms a frame (measured 2026-09-25). The HA occupancy sensor wakes Qwen fail-closed.

The den camera is a Luxonis OAK-D Pro on a Jetson Orin Nano Super 8 GB: RGB 1920×1080 at 30 fps, 640×400 depth from on-device stereo at 15 fps, 640×360 previews. IR emitters are off; night depth is about 6% valid.

Live Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 (served since 2026-10-20 under the old alias qwen3-vl-30b; source still names Qwen3-VL) gets 2–4 still 640×360 JPEGs over about 3 s, every 4 s at most, one request in flight, and returns 10 closed-enum lab-live-scene-1 facts. Live facts end to end: 1.25 s median, 1.97 s p95 (n=21), for whole-room stills; that receipt does not qualify a per-person workload. A 4-frame clip alone took 0.54 s median (n=6, offline, 2026-10-23). vLLM holds about 48 GB.

In the den activity loop (held at operator_stop since 2026-10-21 apart from short owner-approved windows, R5), the activity call is made downstream of Qwen by a third-party cloud judge (JEV jev-1.13.0) from words only, smoothed by an HMM with hysteresis, as one of seven classes. It is shown here only as a note, never as an arbiter; on 2026-10-20 it mostly answered insufficient_evidence.

The den activity loop (YOLO26s + RTMPose-m + same-frame depth lifting + an approximate camera-to-room alignment) is held at operator_stop since 2026-10-21/22 and ran only in short owner-approved windows; in the 10-22 window 115 of 228 detector results expired (capture to completion about 1.46 s). The owner stopped all den, Qwen and backend work on 2026-10-25.
A lab fast-skeleton path (YOLO26s on the LA GPU, RTMPose on CPU, paired depth) sustained about 4.6–4.9 Hz with camera-to-GPU latency p50 284–460 ms; seated, a median of 5 of 17 joints were supported.

There is no multi-person tracker in the den's live path: person events carry a per-frame 'slot-N' id with no cross-frame association; a 2D IoU association exists only for the Home viewing panel, and a sole-reader binding covers exactly one person. LA has a per-person Kalman spatial-tracker (0 tracks on 2026-09-25). Face recognition is excluded by design at Victoria; people are anonymous tracks with explicit profile binding. Two-person tracking is the first post-MVP ticket (AL-P1).
No mmWave is installed: an Everything Presence Pro (LD2450 radar + SEN0609 + PIR) and an Inovelli mmWave switch were ordered on 2026-10-18 for lights-off arrival and vacancy.

A frozen V-JEPA 2.1 ViT-B lab worker with trained heads runs on the LA GPU for Lab recordings only; the always-on loop has excluded it since 2026-10-19. Den probes: computer_work F1 0.93–0.98, reading below the sample gate, no sofa data. The 2026-10-20 research advises against more reading probes because reading is object- and state-defined.

The den has a Scaniverse scan (mesh + splat) in the z_up_metric_floor0 frame, activated for viewing 2026-10-15, scale checked against the owner's measured spans (the scan pack records them as tape measures: length 4.572 m, width 3.759 m, height 2.438 m; within 1%, passed 2026-10-14). Every OAK-to-scan registration (depth ICP, photometric atlas, landmark PnP) was refused; the camera uses a presentation-only approximate placement, and the room mapper has never saved a map.

Fixture models: engineered_gimbal_v1 has a 20° spot (Carclo 10511) on a ±180°/±90° gimbal and six radial zones with orientation_calibration {anchor_zone, anchor_world_angle_deg, order, fine_adjust_deg}; engineered_den_fixture_v1 adds a downlight ring and per-field provenance, all assumed except the spot beam. The planned C12 hardware has 24 channels per fixture (six radial and one down zone, each warm/neutral/cool, plus three spot channels) and is not commissioned; there is no physical command path.

Aiming math exists: solveAim (inverse kinematics) and beamTrace (a centre ray plus 48 rim rays against the collision mesh). In LA, light footprints are drawn by hand in the /spatial tool: the camera-measured footprint calibration was abandoned after three failed runs (auto-exposure and ambient light). The den has no measured footprints.

The lighting brain (AL-1, rules v1.1, Python standard library) runs on the LA box at :8101, deployed 2026-10-20: it sets ambient level and colour for four virtual den fixtures and a reading spot aimed by an over-shoulder planner, keeps the newest 20 decisions with a 'why', pauses a fixture on a manual change, and gives 2+ people ambient only. Output is virtual only. The deployed release (f05bd86d) predates main's bound-reading rule (4fa86f46), which also requires activity and pose bound to one reader; the installed release was not re-verified on 2026-10-25.

The den's four physical Hue bulbs are run by the den_lighting Home Assistant integration (installed 2026-10-27; manifest 1.0.4 in source on 2026-10-28): occupancy on/off with a 120 s vacancy-off, a Steam gaming scene (brightness 38/255 at each bulb's warmest white), and per-fixture manual holds detected from HA Context ids and service-call events. A hold covers only the changed bulb; the others stay automatic. Outside a game a hold ends 120 s after the later of vacancy start and the latest touch, and a manual level also becomes that bulb's normal scene, even while paused. During a game a hold ends at the game's end, and vacancy turns held bulbs off without ending their holds. Game exit clears every hold and restores the pre-game normal snapshot; resume_automatic clears holds and drives each bulb to its current normal. Before each call it re-checks its revision and the light's current target, retries only while that target is unchanged, cancels pending readback on a person's command, and repairs a late report of its own old write once. These are source and dated receipts, not live state.

A virtual den (lab, untracked or on a branch) maps context to scenes, requests and lighting-decision-1 records with hard constraints (envelope, line of sight, eye boxes, quiet) and weighted costs; its physics sums direct light and one diffuse wall bounce with all photometry assumed, and saves corrections bound to their run, decision, fixture and target.

LA's older Living Lights stack has an 8-state classifier per zone, Adaptive Lighting for colour (2000 K at night to 4000 K at midday), manual-touch detection from HA context user and parent ids plus predicted-vs-actual brightness, and JSONL decision and override ledgers.

No lux sensor or blinds control feeds any lighting logic. Daylight appears only as the sun above or below the horizon, a fixed night window in the brain, LA's Adaptive Lighting curve, and an untracked NOAA preview. The Lit view's lux is modeled and labelled not photometric.

No student or distillation exists. V-JEPA tuning uses label tiers (gold, owner, weak = Qwen+JEV agreement) where weak labels train but never score, and a label never scores an arm that consumed its source. A 2026-10-08 rule forbids pseudo-labels in calibrated heads. Den gold is under a minute, all computer_work.

The LA AI host (Ryzen 9 9950X, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, 97,887 MiB) serves one shared vLLM endpoint for voice, camera chat, Intelligence and the den perceiver, beside speech models and a leased V-JEPA worker. vLLM has no priority scheduling. The LA pilot keeps camera chat ahead of live Qwen on separate workers and refuses live Qwen with 429 whenever vLLM reports a waiting request, three or more running, or metrics older than 1 s; a thermal ladder refuses live work at GPU 77 °C or Tctl 88 °C. Voice goes to vLLM directly, past the pilot, so one voice request in flight does not by itself stop a live request.

Room-frame 'room facts' (position zone, looking_at by head pose, hands_near, posture, motion) are built in the Lab but not selected: the configured wire is den-facts-7. They are the nearest existing thing to person-state fields.

Accepted decisions that constrain this design: one engagement authority per room, stable scenes with adaptive delivery, continuous spatial context (ADR 0005–0007, 2026-10-14, accepted in local, untracked files; origin/main's decision index lists only ADR-001 to 004); LA is trusted compute and 'cloud' means third parties; anonymous tracking with explicit profile binding; basic local behavior must survive the loss of LA.

Existing latency targets: occupancy edge to first Qwen send p50 ≤ 0.5 s and Qwen request to fact p50 ≤ 1.05 s / p95 ≤ 1.4 s (LA speed plan); the den MVP's spotlight within about 5 s; a later 100 ms physical command cadence (APT-Z03). The earlier 'about 4.2 s scene to fact' was inferred on 2026-10-08 on the previous model, about half of it the wait for the 4 s tick.
